findings.claim: Generated code on netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework targets is deliberately left without ExcludeFromCodeCoverage through the #if guard. The requirement says all generated code, but the ledger records no preference and says to follow the requirement, so the guard is not a defect. This was checked and is fine.

receipt_plan.detail: [L7] netstandard2.0/.NET Framework exclusion answered 'No preference; follow the requirement'. The README documents the limitation.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Unconditional, no setting: the templates add [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] to every generated formatter, resolver and nested helper class. It is guarded by #if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK, there is no opt-out option, snapshots are updated, and the README is updated.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Opt-out setting: same attribute emission, but a generator option (for example a MessagePackGeneratorOptions or MSBuild property) lets users turn the attribute off. The templates would need a flag that wraps the attribute emission in a conditional, and the option would be documented and covered by tests.
